pl-l2d27c4-d1e108.summary: Asks among which goods free choice is contained.

pl-l2d27c4-d1e111.summary: Cites the Retractationes: free choice of will is among middle goods, since we can misuse it, but we cannot live rightly without it; its good use is virtue, found among great goods; since all goods are from God, the good use of free will, which is virtue, is also from God.
claims: Free choice is a middle good.
Its good use is virtue and from God.

pl-l2d27c4-d1e114.summary: Points out the tension: Augustine said the work of virtue is the good use of middle goods, which include free choice, and also that the good use of free choice is virtue; but if it is virtue, it is not the work of virtue, since virtue and its work differ.

pl-l2d27c4.summary: Asks among which goods free choice belongs. Augustine places it among middle goods, since it can be misused yet one cannot live rightly without it; its good use is virtue, a great good, and since all goods are from God, so is the good use of free will. Lombard notes a tension: Augustine called the work of virtue the good use of middle goods, among which free choice is; if the good use of free choice is the work of virtue, it is not virtue, since virtue and its work differ.
claims: Free choice is a middle good.
The good use of free choice is a virtue and a great good.
The good use of free will is from God.
If good use of free choice is the work of virtue, it cannot also be virtue.
